quarterly_data.quarter: Japan Electronic Materials annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report): net sales JPY 29,366 million (+23.2%), operating income JPY 7,249 million (+58.1%), ordinary income JPY 7,177 million (+54.7%), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 5,451 million (+57.8%) - the company's highest sales and profit since its founding. Management attributes the growth to a large expansion of memory probe card sales and, on profit, to the high utilization of its domestic plants. Consolidated ordinary profit margin was 24.4% and ROE 15.5%, against targets of 10% or more for each.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 29,366 million (+23.2%); operating income JPY 7,249 million (+58.1%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Japan Electronic Materials annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor test parts segment, FY2026 (annual securities report): management states that strong demand for leading-edge semiconductors - GPUs for data centers and generative AI and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) - continued; demand for non-memory probe cards was soft, while for memory probe cards the company raised output to meet growing demand for leading-edge semiconductors in Japan and overseas and the needs of its recovering main customers. Full-scale operation of Kumamoto Plant No. 4 (completed the year before last) and continued capex at existing plants lifted production capacity. Segment net sales JPY 29,142 million (+23.5%), segment profit JPY 9,139 million (+51.5%), despite higher costs from up-front investment in future capacity and product strength. Electron tube parts segment: net sales JPY 223 million (-1.2%), segment profit JPY 8 million (-18.9%). The company notes (risk factors) that, amid consolidation among chipmakers and new fab construction led by large chipmakers, the share of its sales taken by specific customers has been rising.
quarterly_data.figure: Segment net sales JPY 29,142 million (+23.5%); segment profit JPY 9,139 million (+51.5%)

quarterly_data.figure: Order backlog JPY 11,783 million (140.7% of the prior year); orders received JPY 32,775 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Japan Electronic Materials annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capex, FY2026 (annual securities report): the group invested JPY 3,866 million, of which JPY 3,807 million in the semiconductor test parts segment to strengthen production capacity. Main domestic sites: Kumamoto works (Kikuchi, Kumamoto; probe card manufacturing and R&D, 474 employees), head office (Amagasaki, Hyogo; probe card manufacturing and R&D, 218 employees) and Sanda Plant (Sanda, Hyogo; probe card manufacturing, 99 employees); overseas probe card plants in Taiwan (Zhubei), Shanghai, California and Chonburi, Thailand.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 3,866 million (JPY 3,807 million in semiconductor test parts)

quarterly_data.quarter: Japan Electronic Materials annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New plant (annual securities report): to strengthen production of M-type probe cards (probe cards using MEMS technology), which it expects to keep growing, and to develop probe cards for next-generation semiconductors, the company resolved in February 2026 to build a new plant in Amagasaki, Hyogo, and is preparing for completion in August 2028. Planned investment for the Amagasaki Plant (probe card production facility and equipment): JPY 12,500 million in total, JPY 1,031 million already paid; start April 2026, completion August 2028 (capacity increase not stated). Management also plans to keep investing up front in staff and in existing plants to raise capacity further.
quarterly_data.figure: Amagasaki new plant JPY 12,500 million; completion August 2028

quarterly_data.quarter: Japan Electronic Materials annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Other planned facility investments at March 31, 2026 (annual securities report), all semiconductor test parts: Kumamoto works probe card production facility JPY 1,159 million (JPY 596 million paid; April 2025 to May 2027); Kumamoto works probe card production equipment JPY 244 million (JPY 155 million paid; March 2026 to September 2027) and JPY 265 million (JPY 181 million paid; October 2025 to October 2026); Sanda Plant probe card production equipment JPY 382 million (JPY 3 million paid; May 2025 to September 2026) and JPY 195 million (June 2026 to December 2027). The company does not state the added capacity, as the investments are for productivity.
quarterly_data.figure: Kumamoto works production facility JPY 1,159 million (April 2025 to May 2027)

quarterly_data.quarter: Japan Electronic Materials annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Targets (annual securities report): under its fiscal 2024-2026 mid-term plan, which aims to grow faster than the market, the company targets consolidated net sales of JPY 33,000 million and consolidated ordinary income of JPY 7,300 million for fiscal 2026, the plan's final year (the year from April 2026 to March 2027, i.e. FY2027 in the graph's fiscal-year convention), as of the plan progress update published May 14, 2026, plus a consolidated ordinary profit margin of 10% or more and ROE of 10% or more. It plans aggressive capex and development investment to strengthen product capability and capacity, to improve the performance, lead times and cost of M-type probe cards, to accelerate development of probe cards for next-generation semiconductors, and to strengthen overseas sales. Management notes that if supply constraints arise across the supply chain while the generative-AI semiconductor market keeps expanding, they could affect the semiconductor market, customers' production plans and its own production.
quarterly_data.figure: Mid-term plan final-year (April 2026 to March 2027) targets: net sales JPY 33,000 million; ordinary income JPY 7,300 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Japan Electronic Materials annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D, FY2026 (annual securities report): JPY 1,681 million, focused on improving the performance of MEMS-based probes and developing substrates for finer and faster semiconductor circuits, probe card assembly and processing technology, development of probe cards for next-generation semiconductors, and performance gains in existing products. Products: cantilever C-type probe cards (CE series) and advanced V-type vertical probe cards (VT, VS, VE series) and M-type MEMS probe cards (MC, ML, MT series).
